name: KNOT
description: KNOT (KNowledge entanglement-Oriented Testbed) is a benchmark for evaluating large language model unlearning under knowledge entanglement. It contains 20,135 question-answer pairs (5,300 forget, 9,818 retain, 5,017 boundary) in three sub-tasks: KNOT-Entity (personal vs. professional knowledge about 290 well-known public figures), KNOT-Concept (harmful vs. legitimate uses of 150 dual-use scientific concepts within the WMDP topic scope), and KNOT-Skill (Racket vs. Python programming). All QA pairs are generated with DeepSeek-V3.2. Every forget item carries a continuous entanglement score and one of four levels (Low, Medium, High, Extreme).
citeAs: @inproceedings{li2026knot, title={KNOT: A Knowledge Entanglement Benchmark for Robust Unlearning Evaluation}, author={Li, Mengyang and Wang, Jingwen and Zhang, Yu and Liu, Shuang and Zhang, Zhong}, booktitle={Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 39 (NeurIPS 2026), Evaluations and Datasets Track}, year={2026}}
rai:dataCollection: All QA pairs are generated with DeepSeek-V3.2 (API model deepseek-chat). KNOT-Entity: the model is prompted to list well-known real people in six occupation groups (scientist, politician, artist, athlete, business leader, other); for each person it returns two to three personal facts and two to three professional facts as triples in the Wikidata property schema, plus a biography of about 100 words. 290 complete profiles are kept. Forget QA pairs (personal facts), retain QA pairs (professional facts), and boundary QA pairs (requiring both) are then generated from these triples and biographies. No external knowledge base is queried and no Wikipedia text is read; the profiles reflect the generator's knowledge of these public figures. KNOT-Concept: 150 dual-use scientific concepts within the WMDP topic scope (biosecurity, cybersecurity, chemistry) are generated, and for each concept the model produces forget QA pairs about harmful applications, retain QA pairs about legitimate uses, and boundary QA pairs about the shared mechanism. KNOT-Skill: forget QA pairs about Racket programming, retain QA pairs about Python programming, and boundary QA pairs about cross-language translation and shared functional idioms.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: No external raw data is redistributed. The raw model responses used to build KNOT-Entity profiles are included in the code repository under dataset/knot_data/raw/.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: (1) Near-duplicate removal with MinHash LSH (Jaccard threshold 0.8, 128 permutations). (2) LLM factual verification of forget and boundary pairs with DeepSeek-V3.2; pairs not judged correct with confidence at least 0.7 are dropped. Retain pairs are deduplicated but not LLM-verified. (3) Human verification of a stratified 10% sample.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Three graduate-student annotators performed three tasks: (A) factual correctness and (B) set membership (forget/retain/boundary) on the same stratified 10% sample (2,014 items), and (C) entanglement degree on a 1-5 scale on a separate sample of 500 forget items. A guideline document with worked examples was provided and two pilot rounds were used for calibration. Mean Cohen's kappa for set membership is 0.72 across the three sub-tasks.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: In-house annotation interface at the authors' institution; no crowdsourcing platform.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Spearman correlation between human entanglement ratings and the automatic entanglement score is 0.79 on the 500-item validation sample.
rai:annotationsPerItem: Machine annotation for every item (verification, entanglement score for forget items); human annotation for the 10% sample and the 500-item validation sample.
rai:annotatorDemographics: Three graduate students in computer science recruited from the authors' institution, paid at the local graduate-research-assistant hourly rate.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: DeepSeek-V3.2 (deepseek-chat) for profile and QA generation, factual verification, and the LLM-judged dependency score of KNOT-Concept; sentence-transformers all-MiniLM-L6-v2 for embedding similarity; NetworkX for the knowledge-triple structural score of KNOT-Entity; Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct for cross-LLM verification on a 5% sample.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Hosted on HuggingFace Datasets with code on GitHub. The authors will maintain the dataset with versioned releases under semantic versioning; errors and removal requests can be reported through GitHub issues.
rai:dataLimitations: (1) KNOT-Skill is small (254 QA pairs) and should be used as a diagnostic, not for fine-grained method ranking. (2) KNOT-Entity profiles are LLM-generated and may contain factual errors despite verification; they are likely skewed toward Western and Anglophone public figures. (3) Retain pairs are not LLM-verified. (4) The knowledge-triple component of the Entity score is non-zero for only 17.3% of forget items, so for most Entity items the score is determined by embedding similarity alone. (5) Entanglement scores and levels are provided for forget items only. (6) All tasks are QA-format.
rai:dataBiases: (1) KNOT-Entity reflects which public figures the generator considers well known, with likely overrepresentation of Western, English-speaking figures. (2) KNOT-Concept is limited to the WMDP topic scope (biosecurity, cybersecurity, chemistry). (3) KNOT-Skill covers a single programming-language pair.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: KNOT-Entity contains LLM-generated personal information about widely documented real public figures, such as place of birth or residence, family members, marital status, habits, and occasionally health or beliefs. Some statements may be inaccurate. No private contact, financial, or biometric information is included. The data is intended to model privacy-deletion scenarios; users are asked not to use it to re-identify, profile, or harass any individual.
rai:safetyReport: KNOT-Concept contains questions about harmful applications of dual-use concepts within the WMDP topic scope. Items are intended to be conceptual rather than operational. Users are asked not to use the dataset for capability uplift and should follow their institutional safety policies.
rai:dataUseCases: Intended use: evaluating LLM unlearning methods under graded knowledge entanglement, reporting FQ, MU, Boundary Precision, and Boundary Recall per entanglement level (Boundary Recall is not defined for KNOT-Concept). Not validated for: measuring unlearning safety of deployed systems, side-channel leakage, or non-QA behaviors. KNOT scores should not be read as deployment-readiness signals.
rai:dataSocialImpact: Positive: more realistic evaluation of LLM unlearning for privacy deletion and hazardous-knowledge removal, discouraging overclaiming based on benchmarks with little forget/retain entanglement. Risks: good KNOT scores may give false confidence; dual-use content could be misused out of context; generated personal statements about real people could be inaccurate. Mitigations: per-level reporting, conceptual (non-operational) Concept items, a non-binding use request in the dataset card, and a channel for corrections and removals via GitHub issues.
rai:dataSyntheticInformation: All QA pairs, KNOT-Entity profiles, and KNOT-Concept concept descriptions are generated by DeepSeek-V3.2. KNOT-Entity concerns real public figures, and its content reflects the generator's knowledge of them rather than text copied from any source. Entanglement scores are computed algorithmically (embedding similarity, knowledge-triple structural score, and an LLM-judged dependency score) and quantile-discretized into four levels over forget items.

rai:dataSourceDatasets.name: WMDP
rai:dataSourceDatasets.description: Topic scope reference for KNOT-Concept (biosecurity, cybersecurity, chemistry). No WMDP questions are redistributed.

rai:dataProvenanceActivities.name: Entity profile generation
rai:dataProvenanceActivities.description: DeepSeek-V3.2 lists well-known people per occupation group in batches of ten and returns personal and professional triples (Wikidata property schema) and a short biography for each; 290 complete profiles are kept.

rai:dataProvenanceActivities.name: QA generation
rai:dataProvenanceActivities.description: DeepSeek-V3.2 generates forget, retain, and boundary QA pairs for each sub-task from the profiles, concept descriptions, or skill specifications.

rai:dataProvenanceActivities.name: Deduplication and verification
rai:dataProvenanceActivities.description: MinHash LSH deduplication (Jaccard 0.8); DeepSeek-V3.2 factual verification of forget and boundary pairs (confidence at least 0.7); human verification of a stratified 10% sample; Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct cross-check on a 5% sample.

rai:dataProvenanceActivities.name: Entanglement scoring
rai:dataProvenanceActivities.description: For each forget item: maximum cosine similarity to retain items with all-MiniLM-L6-v2 embeddings; for KNOT-Entity, a per-entity knowledge-triple structural score (shared objects, bridging entities, or content-word Jaccard); for KNOT-Concept, a DeepSeek-V3.2 dependency rating (1-5, divided by 5) averaged over five sampled retain questions. Available components are averaged and assigned to four levels at the 25th/50th/75th percentiles within each sub-task.
